## Added

- **Report PDFs can now include their charts.** Every report's **Export** menu
  has a new **Include charts in PDF** tickbox, on by default. With it ticked, a
  PDF export opens with pictures of the report's charts — in the order they
  appear on screen — followed by the usual data table. Untick it for a data-only
  PDF; your choice is remembered on your device.

  The charts reflect whatever filters, grouping and dates are in force when you
  export, so the PDF matches the report you were actually looking at. A panel
  currently showing no data is simply left out rather than exporting as an empty
  box.

- **Charts always print on a light background**, whichever theme you use, so a
  report exported in dark mode looks the same as one exported in light mode. If
  you use dark mode you'll see the charts flick to light for a moment while the
  file is prepared — that's the export being captured, and it puts itself back.

## Fixed

- A section heading in a multi-section PDF could be left stranded at the foot of
  one page with its content on the next.
- A tall image in a PDF ran off the bottom of the page instead of being scaled to
  fit, and sat against the left margin instead of centred.
- A PDF made up only of charts chose portrait orientation, because the page
  layout was decided purely from table column counts and ignored everything else.

## Updated

- The Export menu now closes when you click away from it, which it previously
  didn't.
- Report PDFs are laid out by the same generator the whole-page report export
  uses, so they gain a proper document title and a heading above the data table.
  Previously the title was derived from the filename. **CSV and Excel exports are
  unchanged** — same columns, same values, same sheet layout — so anything that
  consumes them, including scheduled exports, carries on working exactly as
  before.

## Notes

Charts are a PDF-only feature. CSV is a plain-text format that cannot hold a
picture, and the spreadsheet writer used for `.xlsx` files cannot embed one, so
those two formats ignore the setting entirely.

This applies to exports you run from the browser. **Scheduled exports**
(delivered by email, Google Drive, Box or OneDrive) are generated on the server,
where there is no browser to draw a chart in, so they remain tabular.
